core.title: URN wagon and feature segments are the plan's exact kebab-case identifiers
core.given: A source file carries the profile's source URN binding with a well-formed component URN (new or existing)
core.when: the file is written, edited or checked
core.then: The wagon and feature segments MUST be the plan's exact identifiers for the feature that owns the code and MUST match `^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$`.
prefer: During GREEN: derive both values from the feature currently being implemented.
During GREEN: if the identity is already correct, normalize only casing or separators.
avoid: Touching the name, side or layer segments while fixing wagon/feature.
Inventing or renaming plan wagons/features to satisfy the binding.
Copying identifiers from a neighboring feature without checking ownership.
unless: URNs that are not well-formed per the profile's component URN shape (owned by the URN well-formedness rule).
Name, side and layer segments (own rules).
core.why: Wagon and feature are case- and separator-sensitive join keys into the plan artifacts: `Orders` and `orders` differ to a string match, so a wrong binding binds to nothing while reading correctly to a human (silent join failure). Kebab-case is the plan's own grammar.
evidence: The traceability check that realizes this rule reports no wagon/feature finding for the file.
Wagon and feature segments match the plan's canonical identifiers.
The current behavioral acceptance passes (the phase-loop proof).
verification: The observer parses the profile's source URN binding and recognizes a well-formed component URN; the rule applies to existing bindings as well as newly written or edited ones — no diff or phase precondition.

Apply the kebab identifier pattern `^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$` — the plan's own grammar for wagon and feature names — to the wagon and feature segments of a well-formed source URN (segment positions per the profile's component URN shape); the finding names whichever segment(s) fail.
Skip URNs that are not well-formed per the profile's component URN shape; those are owned by the URN well-formedness rule.
Do not evaluate the name, side or layer segments here; they are governed by their own rules.
Severity 3; disposition strict: the checker fails on every finding; there is no advisory mode and no ratchet baseline.

Term silent_join_failure: the state where a binding reads correctly to a human but binds to nothing because a case- or separator-sensitive key did not match. Flag bindings whose segments differ from the plan key only in case or separators.

A pattern pass is not sufficient: canonical identity — the segments equal the plan's identifiers for the feature that owns the code — must also hold. This needs a plan lookup; until a plan-join observer exists it is judged by an LLM/reviewer.

A finding from this rule's check naming the wagon or feature segment is one activation route, not a prerequisite: the rule also applies when the segments pass the pattern but differ from the plan's canonical identifiers.

values: plan wagon/feature identity of the URN

fires: A source file carries the profile's source URN binding (new or pre-existing) whose wagon segment has uppercase letters.
The URN's feature segment uses underscores, camelCase or a leading digit instead of lowercase kebab-case.
The wagon/feature segments match the pattern but are not the plan's identifiers for the feature that owns the code (e.g. copied from a neighboring feature).
The traceability check that realizes this rule reports a finding naming the wagon or feature segment.
doesNotFire: The URN does not have the profile's well-formed component URN shape (owned by the URN well-formedness rule).
Only the name, side or layer segment is malformed; wagon and feature already match the plan's kebab identifiers.
A file with no URN binding.

profileRequirements.bunValue: a well-formed six-segment URN in the source traceability header; segment 1 = wagon, segment 2 = feature; name, side and layer are further segments governed by their own rules

neutralityNotes: The obligation itself (kebab pattern `^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$` plus canonical identity against the plan's identifiers) is plan grammar, not stack grammar, so it stays in the core. What could not be neutralized: (1) the concrete URN shape (six segments, wagon = segment 1, feature = segment 2) and the header-comment binding are per-stack data, carried by urn.component and urn.binding.component; (2) detector/validator and finding ids (bun_green_traceability_detector, GREEN-URN-003, BUN-GREEN-URN-WAGON-FEATURE-001) and the sibling rule id coder.bun.green-urn-pattern are realization details and remain bunOnly, with the core naming the checks generically; (3) the closed activation-fact vocabulary has no 'language' fact, so the Bun language fact is realized as profile scoping (tooling.languages) plus a bunOnly entry; (4) severity 3 and the strict disposition are per-rule data kept in core:verification, per the vocabulary's notProfileKeys.
